Thank you for your patience. ::: :::: The original files in `_labs/lab3` are below: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fs::dir_tree(path = "_labs/lab3/") ## _labs/lab3/ ## ├── app-api.R ## ├── app-api.py ## ├── eda-db.qmd ## ├── model-db.qmd ## ├── py-data-load.py ## └── r-data-load.R ``` ::: In the previous labs, we build a model API with [`vetiver`](https://rstudio.github.io/vetiver-python/stable/) (also [available in R](https://rstudio.github.io/vetiver-r/)). This lab continues with accessing databases and using APIs. I've split these files into separate folders (i.e., projects) and included RStudio project files: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fs::dir_tree(path = "_labs/lab3/Python/") ## _labs/lab3/Python/ ## ├── Python.Rproj ## ├── app-api.py ## ├── model-db.qmd ## └── py-data-load.py ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fs::dir_tree(path = "_labs/lab3/R/") ## _labs/lab3/R/ ## ├── R.Rproj ## ├── app-api.R ## ├── eda-db.qmd ## └── r-data-load.R ``` ::: ## APIs Let's back up a bit and get an understanding of what an API does. In general, APIs are the digital plumbing that makes modern software ecosystems possible. ```{mermaid} %%| fig-cap: 'APIs' %%| fig-align: center %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "fontSize":"16px"}}}%% graph LR DS["Data Scientist"] --> Req["API Request"] Req --> ApiServ["API Server"] ApiServ --> DataProcMod["Data Processing/Model"] DataProcMod --> Res["Results"] Res --> ApiServ ApiServ --> APIResp["API Response"] APIResp --> DS style ApiServ fill:#e1f5fe style DataProcMod fill:#f3e5f5 ``` APIs have standardized language that allows different software systems to communicate and share functionality (without needing to understand how the internal implementation works). **What do they communicate?** 1. What you can request (endpoints) 2. How to make the request (HTTP methods, parameters) 3. What you'll get back (response format) 4.
